vulnerability.name: CVE-2024-51744
vulnerability.description: Improper error handling in github.com/golang-jwt/jwt/v4 ParseWithClaims: a caller inspecting only jwt.ErrTokenExpired can overlook a co-reported jwt.ErrTokenSignatureInvalid.

statements.impact_statement: The advisory affects github.com/golang-jwt/jwt/v4 below v4.5.1. No golang-jwt module of any major version is present in FosterStack Cache: it is absent from go.sum, absent from the compiled package set, and absent from the dependency manifest embedded in the released binaries. golang-jwt/jwt/v5 appears in the module requirement graph only as a transitive requirement of packages of prometheus/client_golang and prometheus/common that this project does not import, and v5 is not affected by this advisory in any version range. Independently reproducible: `go version -m fscache` on any released binary lists the complete set of linked dependencies, and `govulncheck ./...` reports no vulnerabilities.
statements.action_statement: No action required. The affected component is not a dependency of this product, so no upgrade applies.
statements.status_notes: Raised by Snyk against the go.mod project as a module-graph finding. Verified against the shipped v0.1.0 binaries on 2026-09-07.

vulnerability.name: CVE-2026-111943
vulnerability.description: Go standard library crypto/x509: Certificate.Verify did not reject a denylist of known-compromised intermediate certificates (fixed in Go 1.26.10 and 1.27.3).

statements.impact_statement: Applies to the repository-wide cache product with the Go standard library 1.27.2 as the subcomponent: any image of that repository whose Go standard library is 1.27.2 is covered, and an image built with another Go version is not and re-trips the scanner. The evidence below was gathered from, and covers, the nine v0.2.2 image digests (the index, the linux/amd64 image and the linux/arm64 image of each of the production, -fips and -debug variants of ghcr.io/fosterstack/cache); it was not gathered for any other image. The advisory's vulnerable symbol is crypto/x509 Certificate.Verify. Evidence from the images: the fscache binary (fscache-fips in the -fips variant) was extracted from each of the six platform images in the registry; `go version -m` shows Go 1.27.2 and vcs.revision 0ac0586dc1b2de70318b82469fa5b35bfa090068 (tag v0.2.2) with vcs.modified=false, so every image holds that exact source (the -fips binaries also embed GOFIPS140=v1.0.0). govulncheck v1.9.0 -mode=binary lists x509.Certificate.Verify as present in all six binaries; binary mode does not decide whether it is called, so reachability is decided on that embedded source. The FosterStack v0.2.2 server imports neither crypto/tls nor crypto/x509 in its own non-test code, has no HTTP client there and serves plain HTTP (ListenAndServe), so nothing in it verifies a certificate chain (vulnerable_code_not_in_execute_path). Independently reproducible: build govulncheck v1.9.0 with Go 1.27.3, check out commit 0ac0586dc1b2de70318b82469fa5b35bfa090068 and run `GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.27.2 govulncheck -mode=source ./...` (with GOFIPS140=v1.0.0 for the -fips variant, and with GOARCH=amd64 and GOARCH=arm64): each run reports 0 vulnerabilities affecting the code and lists GO-2026-6809 only as a vulnerability in an imported package that the code does not call. Assessed 2026-11-07 against the vulnerability database updated 2026-11-05. This is a claim about these images' execution path, not about crypto/x509 in general, and it needs re-checking whenever the call graph changes.
statements.action_statement: No action is required: the vulnerable function is not called by these images. A build with Go 1.27.3 or later removes the finding; the v0.2.2 images were built with Go 1.27.2.
